subject: gk
question: According to Article ____ no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
solution:
The correct answer is __**28**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 28** of the Indian Constitution prohibits the provision of religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.
 
• However, there is an exception for institutions established under endowments or trusts that mandate the provision of religious instruction.
 
• The prohibition under Article 28 ensures secularism and the separation of religion from state-funded educational institutions.
 
• This article is part of the larger framework of **Fundamental Rights**, specifically under the "Right to Freedom of Religion" (Articles 25-28).
 
• The aim is to ensure that no state-funded institution forces or promotes any specific religious instruction, maintaining neutrality in matters of religion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Secularism in India:** India follows a model of positive secularism, meaning all religions are treated equally, and the state does not favor or discriminate against any religion.
 
• **Exceptions in Article 28:** Religious instruction is allowed in institutions established under specific religious endowments or trusts, provided participation in such instruction is voluntary.
 
• **Other Related Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 25:** Ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.
 
• **Article 26:** Grants every religious denomination the right to manage its religious affairs.
 
• **Article 27:** Prohibits the use of tax proceeds for promoting or maintaining any particular religion.
 
 
 
• **Educational Institutions in India:** The categorization includes state-funded, privately funded, and minority institutions. Only state-funded institutions are subject to the restrictions of Article 28.
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:** The Supreme Court of India has upheld Article 28's provisions as a critical element of India's secular framework in cases such as *S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994)*.
